text: Eleven days after its boss quit, Nvidia hired him back, and its stock jumped more than thirty percent in one morning.
Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in nineteen ninety three. For over thirty years, the leather jacket on stage was the company.
And then, on November the twelfth, he stepped down.
Reports said one of his relationships was with a woman American officials suspected of spying for China. China denied it.
The FBI, Congress and Nvidia's own board all started asking questions.
Without him, the stock fell to its lowest close in sixteen months, and one big bank cut its price target in half.
Fans signed a petition to bring him back. More than a hundred and seventy thousand of them.
The board said it wasn't even considering it.
Then on Monday morning, the same board voted, unanimously, to give him his job back.
Luckily, the President said he had called the board himself. Unluckily, the investigation is still going.
Why forgive so fast? Because to many investors, Nvidia isn't a chip company. It's one man's plan.
It's like a restaurant losing its famous chef. The kitchen is the same, but people stop booking tables.
By lunch, Nvidia was worth close to a trillion dollars more, and the whole market jumped with it.
Eleven days, one exit, one comeback. The most valuable thing Nvidia owns might not be a chip. It's a leather jacket.
